description:
SOMOS ESTUDIANTES DE LA CARRERA PROFESIONAL DE INGENIERÍA DE SISTEMAS EN LA UNIVERSIDAD NACIONAL DE CAJAMARCA QUE BUSCAN DISEÑAR SOLUCIONES TECNOLÓGICAS QUE APORTEN DE MANERA POSITIVA AL PLANETA.

"USAMOS EL FUEGO DE LA TECNOLOGÍA PARA PROTEGER NUESTRO PLANETA".
summary:
PROMETEO-9 is a geospatial web application designed to harmonize historical fire records from NASA's MODIS and VIIRS satellites (FIRMS). It addresses the challenge of heterogeneity in satellite data by creating a consistent time series that allows emergency managers and scientists to visualize historical patterns, anomalies, and trends.
The tool integrates an interactive 3D map where users can draw areas of interest (AOI) to filter data in real-time, a "heatmap" style burning activity calendar that displays intensity by year, month, and day, and an early warning system based on machine learning (KNN) that predicts fire risk. Featuring a "control center" (HUD) interface design, PROMETEO-9 not only visualizes the past but empowers responders to anticipate future crises, fulfilling NASA's goal of improving the global wildfire response through the use of open data.
details:
What does it do and how does it work?
PROMETEO-9 processes and harmonizes historical datasets from NASA FIRMS (MODIS and VIIRS) to create a unified fire activity calendar. Users can navigate a 3D satellite map (MapLibre GL) and draw an Area of Interest (AOI). By doing so, the application instantly filters the backend data (FastAPI + DuckDB), updating a control panel with real-time metrics (active hotspots, FRP, alerts), time-series charts, and a heatmap calendar. It also includes a tactical fire radar and an Artificial Intelligence model (KNN) that predicts the probability of fire recurrence in a selected area.

What benefits does it offer?
It provides emergency managers with a consistent view of fire history, eliminating sensor bias. It allows users to quickly identify critical months, compare current activity against historical averages (anomalies), and download CSV reports, streamlining decision-making and resource allocation.

What tools and languages were used?

  • Frontend: React (Vite), TailwindCSS/Pure CSS, Recharts (data visualization), MapLibre GL JS (3D map), Mapbox GL Draw (polygon drawing).
  • Backend: Python, FastAPI, DuckDB (for ultra-fast queries on Parquet files), Scikit-Learn (KNN model).
  • Data: NASA FIRMS (MODIS and VIIRS).

In what sense is it creative?
The creativity lies in fusing a futuristic user interface (sci-fi HUD style, featuring a tactical radar, glassmorphism effects, and an AI mascot) with a high-performance backend. Furthermore, the ability to interact with the map by drawing areas and watching all charts and AI predictions update in real time transforms a boring data table into an immersive satellite monitoring experience.
dataRefs: NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System)
